## Recommendation
- **Go to Grand Haven first (3 of 4).** Boat fishing there was rated good in the newest report.
- **South Haven or St. Joseph are the backups (2 of 4 each).** South Haven was rated average. St. Joseph had a good bite but no quality rating, and its water was the warmest.
- **Muskegon last (1 of 4).** Its newest report rated boat fishing slow because of warm water.
- **At any of them, start around 85-130 ft of water and run lines about 50-90 ft down.** Use green or blue glow spoons and white flasher-fly combinations.
- **Check the wind before you launch.** I couldn't get a wind forecast, and gusts reached 20-38 mph at these ports last week.

## Why
- **Grand Haven ranks first:** the Aug 12 Grand Haven report rated boat fishing good, with salmon 50-90 ft down in 85-150 ft of water (Grand Haven, 2026-08-12).
- **Muskegon ranks last:** the same week's Muskegon boat report was slow, and anglers blamed the warm water (Muskegon, 2026-08-12).
- **Pick depths and lures from the reports:** salmon were holding at 45-90 ft down across all four ports, and glow spoons and flasher-fly combos were the lures that worked (Aug 12 bulletin, all four ports).
- **I'd expect the warm water to make the bite patchy this week:** the buoy near Grand Haven averaged about 72 F in the week before today, warmer than the 68 F in the Aug 12 report. Chinook prefer 52-58 F (NY DEC guidance), so I'd expect fish to be deeper or scattered.

## Evidence
**Recent reports** (newest is the Aug 12 bulletin, 6 days old)
- Grand Haven, boat: quality 3 (good). Salmon 50-90 ft down in 85-150 ft of water; "Blue and green spoons worked well, along with a white flasher-fly combo" (Grand Haven, 2026-08-12).
- Grand Haven, pier: slow. "Due to increasing water temperatures, no salmon or steelhead were reported from the pier" (Grand Haven, 2026-08-12).
- South Haven, boat: quality 2 (average). "A fair number of salmon were reported 45 to 90 feet down in 100 to 130 feet of water"; green or blue glow spoons worked (South Haven, 2026-08-12).
- St. Joseph, boat: not rated. Salmon and a few steelhead 55-80 ft down in 90-120 ft of water; white flasher-fly combinations and glow spoons "produced the most bites" (St. Joseph, 2026-08-12). Not rated means a weak positive.
- Muskegon, boat: quality 0 (slow). Salmon 50-85 ft down in 100-140 ft; "Anglers targeting salmon were unsuccessful due to warm water" (Muskegon, 2026-08-12).
- Earlier, July 22: Grand Haven boats were rated good on spoons 30-90 ft down, and Muskegon boats were average (Grand Haven and Muskegon, 2026-07-22).

**Past seasons** (weeks with similar surface water, about 71 F, from prior years; history, not current)
- Boat fishing in similar weeks was usually average to good. Grand Haven rated 3 on 2025-08-13 and 2025-08-20, with the best action 50-110 ft down (Grand Haven, 2025-08-13 and 2025-08-20).
- Piers were usually slow in those weeks, and in 2025 the Grand Haven pier slowed "due to the warmer water temperatures" (Grand Haven, 2025-08-13).
- South Haven and St. Joseph boat fishing in late August ran average, rated 2 (South Haven and St. Joseph, 2025-08-27).

**Conditions now**
- Live conditions didn't come through. The tool returned a backtest summary for the week before Aug 18, not current readings, and it had no modeled cold-layer depth or wind forecast.
- That summary gave buoy surface water of about 72-74 F at Grand Haven, Muskegon, South Haven and St. Joseph, with upwelling-favoring wind on 14-28 hours that week (summary, week before 2026-08-18).
- Upwelling-favoring wind on Muskegon was 28 hours that week, the most of the four ports, and its pier water had risen only slightly. I'd expect that to help the Muskegon bite sooner than the reports show, but I have no report confirming it.

## Caveats
- The newest report is 6 days old, and it shows the water warming fast (buoy up 5-6 F in a week at Grand Haven and Muskegon). Treat the ratings as a guide to what to expect, not a readout of today.
- Every rating rests on one report per port. The Grand Haven 3 comes from a single week.
- Water temps: the buoy readings are measured. I don't have a modeled cold-layer depth for this week, so I can't say how deep the 55 F water is.
- Check the marine forecast and the current wind before launching; it is the one piece I could not get.
